title: Doctrine Of Double Effect
definition: A moral principle that holds that morally licit acts may have foreseeable and inevitable immoral consequences, so long as the immoral consequence is not the direct intention of the actor.

difficulty_levels.beginner: It's like doing a good deed that might accidentally help a bad cause. It's okay if you didn't intend to cause the bad outcome.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The Doctrine of Double Effect is a moral principle derived from the separation of means and ends, where morally licit acts may have foreseeable and unintended immoral consequences.
difficulty_levels.expert: The Doctrine of Double Effect emphasizes the distinction between an act's foreseeable consequences and its intended effects, philosophically connecting to the debates on free will and determinism, and ethically resonating with discussions on utilitarianism and deontology.

extra_fields.insight: The Doctrine of Double Effect highlights the complexities of moral responsibility and the tensions between individual actions and their broader consequences.
